summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 3.17/274)

data.turoyo: Muǧəb du amro di qadišuṯo, d d mʔamarwayle lu faṭəryarxo. Ṭləbwayle qašo ʕAziz li Sənnados Qadəšto b Ḥəməṣ. <...>
data.translation: According to the order which the patriarch had commanded. He had invited Father Aziz to the Holy Synod in Homs, <...>

rationale: First II Preterit-wa box; command and ensuing invitation identify the patriarch as agent. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; analysis rests on the Turoyo.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JL 20.7/52)

data.turoyo: w mu=yawmawo edi u=zlamawo haw ḥzeli w haw mʔamalle aʕli.
data.translation: Und von dem Tag an habe ich den Mann nicht mehr gesehen, und er hat tnir keine Befehle mehr erteilt.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; explicit ʕal-person under command and haw cessation, retaining the edition’s irregular tnir.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (23/48)

data.turoyo: Bu yawmawo mʔamalla laz zamore d oṯən w d maḥti i məštuṯayḏe w bu lalyawo mbaraxla i barṯo aʕle.
data.translation: und noch am selben Tage befahl sie den Musikern, zu kommen und das Hochzeitsfest für ihn zu veranstalten, und in jener Nacht noch ließ sie ihm die Tochter antrauen.

rationale: Fifth Preterit example; female agent -la, l-musician addressee and two d-content clauses in one clear sentence.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; third-person commander and second-person suffix addressee, with relative order content.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (69/121)

data.turoyo: Əmmo: "Kəmʔamrono, d qəṭlatle w moṭatli qadaḥ d admo m diḏe, d šətyalle."

summary: New idiom: mʔamalle/mʔamər: kəmamrət 'zu Befehl! (Höflichkeitsformel)'

data.translation: <...> I say, “At your command, sir! (You command, my superior!)” <...>

rationale: The Turoyo formula explicitly glosses Turkish Emredersin efendim as a deferential acknowledgment. Searches mʔamr and mamr returned conditional command examples but no listed formula. One explicit acknowledgment; 3.36/996 supplies a related request for instructions. English is project machine translation.

summary: All 48 tokens belong to the command homonym ʔmr 2 and stem II; none supplies a new lexical sense, stem or box. Preserve befehlen and the Arabic etymology without rewriting.

Preterit agents use -le/-la/-lux and may be doubled by l-NPs: li maḥkame mʔamalla (24/307) identifies the l-marked court as agent, not the recipient. The entry’s l-u=ʕmiro wording likewise identifies a commander in 35/28.

Persons commanded occur with l- (musicians, gardener), ʕal- (individual servants, soldiers, a bird or ant collective, first-person aʕli), or a pronominal suffix. ʕal- can also mark people affected by a requested ruling (56/103); do not turn all such phrases into an invariant addressee rule.

Content may be a d-/ḥatta d-clause, a relative u mede/mən d, direct quoted directives, or an ensuing action sequence. These are constructions of befehlen, not separate meanings of authorize, rule or speak.

Aspect: ko-/k-Infectum can perform a command (69/121–122, Hors 2/114); conditional Infectum can request or acknowledge authority without asserting a completed order. Preterit haw in JL 20.7/52 excludes further orders after a temporal boundary.
The -r- is retained in mʔamarle and assimilated in mʔamalle; mamrat and maməlle omit or reduce the glottal segment. Record the surface forms without reconstructing missing segments in examples.

Bundled references in the original are comparative attestations, not necessarily claims that every cited verse has the same words. Do not remove 24/51, 24/246, 29/187, 29/486, 36/71 or 61/247 merely because their quoted contexts differ.
Preterit-wa mʔamarwayle adds a box absent after round 1; the l-marked patriarch is the commander, not the commanded person.

Jan supplies an explicit Turkish/Turoyo acknowledgment formula. It belongs in Idiomatic phrases, not the numbered sense list. This supports a contact comparison without proving that the Turoyo use originated as a calque.
Nested commands at 2.4/655 retain the existing II.1 befehlen sense. The speaker asks the guard to tell the chief doctor to command the duty officer to inform the guard.
What controls l- versus ʕal- for a commanded person? The same root permits both, and l-marked commanders must be kept distinct from addressees.
Check 27/44 against the source edition: this input has mʔamalle, while the reader reports mʔamalle-li in an ʔḏʕ quotation. No suffix is silently restored.
At 95/208 the alignment note assigns “wir haben einen weiten Weg vor uns” to the preceding verse. Verify verse alignment before quoting any translation from this occurrence; none is added here.
Confirm the local contraction maməlle at 95/208 and mamrat at 53/58; the command interpretation is supported by their arguments, but no unrecorded base form is created.
Jan 2.16/3548: does kəmamri mean prescribe here, prohibit in context, or belong to ʔmr 1 saying? Provisionally II.1 on morphology; no new prohibition sense or example.
How conventional is kəmamrət as a freestanding acknowledgment across speakers, compared with a literal question Komʔamrat, mən yo? at 3.36/996?

Laws may prescribe an ecclesiastical course and an addressee may deferentially ask what is commanded. No separate prohibit or request sense is established. The actual prohibitive force at 2.16/3548 is contextually inferred and remains uncertain.
